transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Leo Zhang (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM); Mark Li (Aurora - Head of Platform), Sara Torres (Aurora - SRE Lead), Evan Brooks (Aurora - CTO)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Quick follow-up after outage on 2027-09-08 that caused elevated latency and a partial failover for Aurora's Dedicated pool. Discussed root cause (autoscaler + KV cache invalidation), mitigations (hotfix, rollout plan), compensation/SLA credits, and next steps (logs, benchmark, runbook updates).

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this tight, we know you have folks on call already, um this is the follow up to the incident last week - thought we'd run through the timeline, fixes, and next steps.
[00:15] Mark (Aurora): Thanks Samira. appreciate you pulling this together. just so you know we've got the SRE and platform leads here, Sara and I and Evan.
[00:28] Samira: great. quick intro — Leo from our infra team is here to go through the technical timeline and the hotfix we shipped. Priya will coordinate the customer success parts and credits.
[00:40] Leo (Redwood SE): hi all. so, to summarize in one line: we saw an edge case in the Dedicated autoscaler that caused rapid downscales during a short spike of ephemeral requests which in turn triggered a KV cache invalidation path. that then exposed a slower cold-start path for KV warmups and caused tail latency to spike.
[01:05] Sara (Aurora SRE): sorry can you repeat the KV part, you said cash?
[01:10] Leo: yeah sorry, kv cache — the internal key-value cache. there was a sequence where the cache entries were marked stale when the autoscaler removed nodes, and our warmup path didn't refill them quickly enough under Aurora's traffic shape.
[01:26] Evan (Aurora CTO): what about fallbacks? i thought the cluster should have routed to the fallback model variant — why did customers hit 500s?
[01:34] Leo: good q — the routing policy did fallback, but because the node churn coincided with our instance registration delay we had a short window where request routing hit partially-initialized hosts; some requests timed out and retried causing cascading pressure. also one of the health-check thresholds was too strict.
[01:50] Mark: timeline please — when did this start? our monitoring shows first errors at 03:12 UTC on 2027-09-08.
[01:58] Leo: that aligns — spike at 03:10, autoscaler responded within 90s, it removed 6 nodes in two waves, then we saw KV invalidations 30–60s later and elevated p95/p99 from 03:13 to 03:29.
[02:15] Samira: we rolled a hotfix that evening to change the autoscaler cooldown and to guard the KV invalidation so removal is deferred until cache is drained. Leo?
[02:25] Leo: yes. hotfix details: increased autoscaler downscale stabilization from 60s to 300s for Dedicated pools with heavy KV usage, added a pre-termination hook to flush and persist KV segments, and relaxed the health-check to allow a 10s registration grace. we deployed to Aurora cluster at ~22:00 UTC on 2027-09-08.
[02:48] Sara: we saw the errors go down after that, thanks. one outstanding is our concern about single az impact — are those autoscaler decisions AZ-aware?
[02:56] Leo: today autoscaler is region-aware but not deeply AZ-aware; that's a known gap. short term we can pin Dedicated pools to avoid cross-az downscales. longer term we plan an AZ-aware eviction strategy.
[03:10] Evan: okay. from a compliance perspective, we also need the audit logs of scaling events and who triggered what — that helps our postmortem.
[03:19] Priya (Redwood CSM): we'll provide the audit trail; Samira and I will coordinate with your security lead.
[03:25] Samira: report note — we'll include timeline, root cause, what we changed, and the exact list of nodes affected.
[03:32] Mark: can you confirm if encryption or key management were affected? any PII exposure?
[03:38] Leo: no. nothing to indicate data at rest or in flight was exposed. this was an availability issue; KMS/HSM calls were unaffected.
[03:45] Sara: we did notice elevated error rates in the rps->model route, and some retries from clients. that ballooned the queueing.
[03:52] Leo: yes, retry amplification was a factor — client SDK retry default is aggressive and we should update recommended SDK settings for high-churn scenarios.
[04:05] Evan: thanks. what about compensations? our procurement asks about SLA credits.
[04:11] Priya: we can start the SLA credit process — we'll need the exact downtime windows you consider an outage. Samira will send the formal postmortem and then our finance team will calculate credits per the contract.
[04:25] Mark: appreciate it. action on our side: we'll share the top-5 endpoints by traffic and our traffic profile for your benchmark.
[04:33] Samira: perfect. Leo, do you want to walk thru the short-term mitigations vs medium-term roadmap?
[04:40] Leo: short-term (already done or in progress): 1) hotfix to autoscaler cooldown and pre-termination hook (deployed), 2) registration grace to reduce partial host routing (deployed), 3) recommend pinning Dedicated pools to AZs for Aurora's current setup (config change). Medium-term: 1) AZ-aware autoscaler improvements, 2) improved KV warmup path with background refill, 3) synthetic canary traffic to exercise downscale/warmup, 4) richer tracing for KV lifecycle.
[05:20] Sara: for the medium term, can you give a rough ETA?
[05:24] Leo: AZ-aware autoscaler is an engineering project estimate 6-8 weeks; KV warmup improvements 4-6 weeks; canary framework — 3-5 weeks. we can prioritize the KV warmup as highest for Aurora.
[05:35] Mark: okay, parallel ask: can we get a one-off run where Redwood runs Aurora traffic profile on a dedicated test replica? want to reproduce the scenario in controlled env.
[05:44] Samira: yes — next step we'll schedule a benchmark run. Leo, coordinate with Mark for traffic shape.
[05:50] Leo: will do.
[05:55] [06:00] (brief cross talk) Speaker 1: sorry, are we recording the runbook changes?
[06:03] Priya: yes we'll update the runbook and the incident page in the customer portal.
[06:08] Mark: also need the list of configuration flags changed and the commit IDs, that helps our internal auditors.
[06:14] Leo: sure - we'll provide commit hashes, release notes, and the k8s rollout manifests we used.
[06:20] Sara: on monitoring — i want a new dashboard tile for early KV-miss signal, something at p50 and a counter for cache refill rates.
[06:29] Leo: agreed; we'll add that and share the grafana dashboards.
[06:33] Evan: any work on SDK guidance?
[06:36] Samira: yes we will update the SDK best practices doc — recommend backoff, jitter, and shorter connection timeouts for spiky workloads.
[06:45] Mark: question about fallback models — will Redwood do automatic fallbacks to smaller models to keep latency low rather than cold-starting large instances?
[06:52] Leo: we do have model-variant fallbacks; the issue here was that the hosts themselves weren't fully registered so fallback routing still hit unhealthy hosts. after the registration grace fix that should reduce the window. in addition we can add a policy to prefer warm small-variant instances in the event of heavy churn.
[07:10] Priya: on the customer success end, we'll propose credits and timeline. Samira will own the postmortem delivery.
[07:17] Samira: yes I'll send the deck by Friday (2027-09-16). Also we'll include a remediation timeline and our public-facing knowledge base article for runbook steps.
[07:25] Mark: thanks. any blockers from Redwood that we should be aware of?
[07:29] Leo: none immediate — the hotfix is live; medium-term changes require engineering cycles and we'll prioritise Aurora's items.
[07:36] Sara: one more ask: can we get the raw traces for 03:10-03:30 UTC? particularly the pod lifecycle and the proxy logs.
[07:44] Leo: yes we'll pull and share logs, sanitized for PII.
[07:49] Evan: ok. last item — we'd like a follow up meeting in a week to confirm the benchmark results and prioritized roadmap.
[07:56] Samira: we'll set it for 2027-09-23.
[08:00] (wrap) Samira: recap: 1) Samira send postmortem deck by 9/16; 2) Leo to send logs and commit IDs by 9/18; 3) Priya to kick off SLA credit request by 9/17; 4) Mark send traffic profile by 9/16; 5) Benchmark scheduled and follow-up meeting 9/23. Thanks all.
[08:20] Mark: thanks, appreciate it.
[08:24] (call ends)
notes: Incident root cause: autoscaler downscale + KV cache invalidation + registration delay
Hotfix deployed 2027-09-08: increased downscale stabilization, pre-termination hook, registration grace
Medium term: AZ-aware autoscaler, improved KV warmup, synthetic canaries, better tracing
